items.stem: Interventionists in the 1890s and early 1900s argued that the United States had both the right and the responsibility to project power globally. Which of the following best evaluates the strongest logical foundation for the interventionist position?

choices.text: The moral obligation to spread Christianity and democratic values to less-developed societies provided sufficient justification for intervention without any need for strategic or economic arguments.

choices.text: Interventionists built the most persuasive case by combining strategic necessity (sea power and naval bases), economic interests (protecting trade and markets), and moral purpose (spreading democratic values) into a mutually reinforcing framework.
choices.textEs: Los intervencionistas construyeron el caso más persuasivo combinando la necesidad estratégica (poder naval y bases navales), los intereses económicos (proteger el comercio y los mercados) y el propósito moral (difundir los valores democráticos) en un marco mutuamente reforzante.

choices.text: The economic argument that American businesses needed overseas markets was the only logically sound foundation for interventionism, as moral and strategic arguments were mere rationalizations.
choices.textEs: El argumento económico de que las empresas americanas necesitaban mercados de ultramar fue la única base lógicamente sólida para el intervencionismo, ya que los argumentos morales y estratégicos fueron meras racionalizaciones.

choices.text: Interventionists rested their case on the Monroe Doctrine, arguing that European interference in any part of the world threatened American security.

items.stem: Non-interventionists in the 1890s–1910s drew on several different traditions to oppose American expansion. Which of the following best distinguishes between the constitutional argument and the moral argument made by non-interventionists?
items.stemEs: Los no intervencionistas en las décadas de 1890–1910 recurrieron a varias tradiciones diferentes para oponerse a la expansión americana. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones distingue mejor entre el argumento constitucional y el argumento moral planteados por los no intervencionistas?

choices.text: The constitutional and moral arguments against American imperialism were essentially identical in substance because the Constitution was universally understood by anti-imperialists to be a fundamentally moral document grounded in universal natural rights.
choices.textEs: Los argumentos constitucional y moral eran esencialmente idénticos porque la Constitución se entendía como un documento moral basado en derechos naturales.

choices.text: The moral argument focused narrowly on legal technicalities about congressional representation requirements, while the constitutional argument focused primarily on the ethical obligations of more powerful nations toward the peoples they governed.
choices.textEs: El argumento moral se enfocaba en tecnicidades legales sobre la representación en el Congreso, mientras que el argumento constitucional se enfocaba en el tratamiento ético de los pueblos colonizados.

choices.text: The constitutional argument held that no new territory could be legally acquired by the United States without a formal congressional declaration of war, while the moral argument demanded immediate admission of all acquired territories as full states.
choices.textEs: El argumento constitucional sostenía que ningún territorio podía adquirirse sin una declaración formal de guerra, mientras que el argumento moral sostenía que los territorios debían ser admitidos como estados inmediatamente tras la adquisición.

choices.text: The constitutional argument held that governing territories without representation violated American self-government, while the moral argument held that subjugating free peoples violated the natural rights principles in the Declaration of Independence.
choices.textEs: El argumento constitucional sostenía que gobernar territorios sin representación o un camino hacia la estadidad violaba la estructura del autogobierno americano, mientras que el argumento moral sostenía que subyugar a pueblos libres violaba los principios de derechos naturales consagrados en la Declaración de Independencia.

items.explanation: The constitutional argument held that the U.S. government had no legal authority to govern territories permanently without their representation in Congress and without a path to statehood — that the Constitution 'followed the flag.' The moral argument, by contrast, held that regardless of legal technicalities, it was simply wrong to subjugate free peoples, deny them self-determination, and treat them as colonial subjects — this was a violation of the natural rights principles in the Declaration of Independence. These are distinct arguments that could be made independently. Option A conflates the two arguments; Option B reverses them; Option C misrepresents the constitutional argument.

Estas son argumentaciones distintas que podían hacerse de forma independiente. La opción A las confunde; la B las invierte; la C malinterpreta el argumento constitucional.

Which of the following best evaluates which side was more accurate in predicting the consequences of the policy choices made in the 1890s–1910s?
items.stemEs: Los intervencionistas argumentaban que una marina poderosa y presencia en el extranjero protegerían los intereses comerciales americanos, mientras que los no intervencionistas argumentaban que el involucramiento en el extranjero arrastraría a EE. UU. a guerras innecesarias. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor qué lado fue más acertado al predecir las consecuencias de las decisiones políticas tomadas en las décadas de 1890–1910?

choices.text: Interventionists were fully vindicated because U.S. global commercial and strategic engagement consistently produced substantial benefits with minimal negative military, political, or financial consequences for the American public.
choices.textEs: Los intervencionistas quedaron plenamente vindicados porque el compromiso global de EE. UU. produjo beneficios comerciales y ganancias estratégicas con mínimas consecuencias negativas.

choices.text: Non-interventionists were fully vindicated because American overseas expansion produced no lasting commercial benefits and led directly to a series of costly, prolonged military commitments that drained American resources.
choices.textEs: Los no intervencionistas quedaron plenamente vindicados porque la expansión en el extranjero no produjo beneficios comerciales duraderos y condujo directamente a compromisos militares costosos.

choices.text: Both sides had partial validity: interventionists correctly anticipated commercial and strategic benefits, while non-interventionists correctly predicted that global entanglement would draw the U.S. into costly conflicts like the Philippine-American War and WWI.
choices.textEs: Ambos lados tenían validez parcial: los intervencionistas anticiparon correctamente los beneficios comerciales y estratégicos, mientras que los no intervencionistas predijeron correctamente que el involucramiento global arrastraría a EE. UU. a conflictos costosos como la Guerra Filipino-Americana y eventualmente la Primera Guerra Mundial.

choices.text: Neither side's argument can be meaningfully evaluated because the historical events of the early twentieth century were determined by random, unpredictable factors that no political movement or strategic framework could have accurately anticipated.
choices.textEs: Ninguno de los dos lados fue preciso porque los eventos históricos fueron determinados por factores aleatorios que ni los intervencionistas ni los no intervencionistas podían haber anticipado.

items.explanation: Examining the historical record of 1895–1917, both sides had partial validity. Interventionists were correct that a strong navy and overseas presence expanded U.S. commercial reach and strategic influence. Non-interventionists were also partially correct: the Philippine-American War proved far bloodier and longer than anticipated, and U.S. global entanglement contributed to eventual entry into WWI. The honest historical assessment acknowledges that both predictions had merit and both had blind spots. Option A ignores the Philippine-American War and WWI; Option B ignores the genuine commercial benefits; Option D makes an unprovable counterfactual claim.
items.explanationEs: Examinando el registro histórico de 1895–1917, ambos lados tenían validez parcial. Los intervencionistas tenían razón en que una marina fuerte y presencia en el extranjero expandieron el alcance comercial e influencia estratégica de EE. UU. Los no intervencionistas también tenían parcialmente razón: la Guerra Filipino-Americana resultó mucho más sangrienta y larga de lo anticipado, y el involucramiento global de EE. UU. contribuyó a su eventual entrada en la Primera Guerra Mundial. La opción A ignora la Guerra Filipino-Americana y la Primera Guerra Mundial; la B ignora los beneficios comerciales genuinos; la D hace una afirmación contrafactual no comprobable.

items.stem: Andrew Carnegie, a wealthy industrialist, was a prominent member of the Anti-Imperialist League. Which of the following best explains the apparent paradox of a major capitalist opposing American imperialism?
items.stemEs: Andrew Carnegie, un rico industrial, era un prominente miembro de la Liga Anti-Imperialista. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la aparente paradoja de que un importante capitalista se opusiera al imperialismo americano?

choices.text: Carnegie secretly supported American imperialism but joined the Anti-Imperialist League strategically to protect the business interests of his steel and railroad companies in regions the U.S. was considering for colonial annexation.
choices.textEs: Carnegie apoyaba secretamente el imperialismo pero se unió a la Liga Anti-Imperialista para proteger sus intereses comerciales en países que EE. UU. podría colonizar.

choices.text: Carnegie believed commercial access to global markets could be achieved through free trade without the costly burden of colonial administration, making formal imperialism economically inefficient.
choices.textEs: Carnegie creía que el acceso comercial a los mercados globales podía lograrse a través del libre comercio sin la costosa carga de la administración colonial, haciendo al imperialismo económicamente ineficiente desde una perspectiva empresarial.

choices.text: Carnegie opposed imperialism specifically because he feared that overseas economic competition and foreign markets would directly undermine the domestic profitability and market dominance of his American steel operations.
choices.textEs: Carnegie se opuso al imperialismo porque temía que la competencia en el extranjero socavaría la rentabilidad de sus operaciones siderúrgicas nacionales.

choices.text: Carnegie opposed all forms of American commercial expansion — both domestic monopoly and international imperialism — on consistent principled moral and democratic grounds rooted in his reading of the Declaration of Independence.
choices.textEs: Carnegie se opuso a todas las formas de expansión comercial americana, tanto doméstica como internacional, por razones morales de principio.

items.explanation: Carnegie's opposition to imperialism was not paradoxical when understood in its full context. Carnegie believed in free trade and commercial expansion without the burden of colonial administration. He and other business-minded non-interventionists argued that colonies were economically inefficient — they cost more to maintain militarily than they returned in commercial profit — and that American businesses could access global markets through trade agreements rather than territorial control. Additionally, Carnegie was a proponent of the 'Gospel of Wealth' and believed in a specific version of American exceptionalism that he felt was corrupted by empire-building. Option A presents a conspiracy theory not supported by evidence; Option C is partially true but incomplete; Option D misrepresents Carnegie's views.
items.explanationEs: La oposición de Carnegie al imperialismo no era paradójica cuando se entendía en su contexto completo. Carnegie creía en el libre comercio y la expansión comercial sin la carga de la administración colonial. Él y otros no intervencionistas de mentalidad empresarial argumentaban que las colonias eran económicamente ineficientes — costaban más de mantener militarmente de lo que devolvían en beneficio comercial — y que las empresas americanas podían acceder a los mercados globales a través de acuerdos comerciales en lugar del control territorial. La opción A presenta una teoría de conspiración; la C es parcialmente correcta pero incompleta; la D tergiversa las opiniones de Carnegie.

items.stem: Between 1899 and 1902, the United States fought a brutal war against Filipino independence fighters led by Emilio Aguinaldo. Which of the following best explains how this conflict challenged the stated goals of American interventionists?
items.stemEs: Entre 1899 y 1902, Estados Unidos libró una brutal guerra contra los combatientes de la independencia filipina liderados por Emilio Aguinaldo. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor cómo este conflicto desafió los objetivos declarados de los intervencionistas americanos?

choices.text: It proved that the U.S. Army was entirely unprepared for guerrilla insurgency warfare in tropical terrain, directly undermining the strategic argument that American military power could manage overseas colonies efficiently.
choices.textEs: Demostró que el ejército de EE. UU. no estaba preparado para la guerra de guerrillas, socavando el argumento estratégico del imperialismo.

choices.text: It proved conclusively that colonial administration was far more expensive than the economic returns from Philippine markets and raw materials could justify, systematically undermining the economic argument for imperialism.
choices.textEs: Demostró que la administración colonial era más costosa de lo que justificaban los retornos económicos, socavando el argumento económico del imperialismo.

choices.text: It challenged interventionists primarily because American forces suffered unexpectedly high casualties in brutal counter-insurgency operations, making the public question whether the military had adopted the right strategic approach.
choices.textEs: Desafió a los intervencionistas principalmente porque las fuerzas americanas sufrieron bajas inesperadamente altas, haciendo que el público cuestionara la estrategia militar.

choices.text: It directly contradicted the moral justification for imperialism by revealing that the U.S. was using violent suppression against the very people it had claimed to be liberating from Spanish colonial rule.
choices.textEs: Contradijo directamente la justificación moral de la intervención al revelar que EE. UU. usaba la supresión colonial violenta contra las mismas personas que afirmaba estar liberando de la opresión imperial.

items.explanation: American interventionists had justified the Spanish-American War and subsequent territorial acquisition partly by claiming they were liberating oppressed peoples from Spanish colonialism. The Philippine-American War exposed the contradiction: rather than liberating Filipinos, the U.S. was conducting a violent colonial war to prevent them from exercising the self-determination the U.S. had claimed to champion. The tactics used — including water torture and civilian concentration camps — further undermined the moral justification. Option A is partially correct but understates the ideological challenge; Option B describes an economic concern, not the stated goals; Option C misidentifies the challenge as military rather than ideological.
items.explanationEs: Los intervencionistas americanos habían justificado la Guerra Hispano-Americana y la posterior adquisición territorial alegando en parte que estaban liberando a pueblos oprimidos del colonialismo español. La Guerra Filipino-Americana expuso la contradicción: en lugar de liberar a los filipinos, EE. UU. libraba una violenta guerra colonial para evitar que ejercieran la autodeterminación que EE. UU. afirmaba defender. La opción A es parcialmente correcta pero subestima el desafío ideológico; la B describe una preocupación económica; la C identifica incorrectamente el desafío como militar en lugar de ideológico.

items.stem: Senator George Hoar of Massachusetts argued against the Treaty of Paris (1898) on the grounds that American self-government had no right to govern unwilling foreign peoples. Which of the following best evaluates the long-term impact of Hoar's position on U.S. foreign policy?
items.stemEs: El senador George Hoar de Massachusetts argumentó contra el Tratado de París (1898) con el fundamento de que el autogobierno americano no tenía derecho a gobernar a pueblos extranjeros en contra de su voluntad. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el impacto a largo plazo de la posición de Hoar en la política exterior de EE. UU.?

choices.text: Hoar's position failed immediately but contributed to a tradition of principled non-interventionism that resurfaced in later debates, including Wilson's self-determination principle and the eventual path toward Philippine independence.
choices.textEs: La posición de Hoar fracasó a corto plazo pero contribuyó a una tradición de no intervencionismo principista que resurgiría en futuros debates, incluido el principio de autodeterminación de Wilson y el eventual camino hacia la independencia filipina.

choices.text: Hoar's position succeeded in the immediate term: the Senate ultimately rejected the Treaty of Paris, the Philippines were not colonized, and Filipino independence was granted within three years of the Spanish-American War.
choices.textEs: La posición de Hoar tuvo éxito a corto plazo, ya que el Senado rechazó el Tratado de París y las Filipinas no fueron colonizadas.

choices.text: Hoar's position had no meaningful long-term impact because anti-imperialist arguments were permanently and decisively discredited after the successful conclusion of U.S. military campaigns throughout the Philippine archipelago.
choices.textEs: La posición de Hoar no tuvo impacto a largo plazo porque los argumentos anti-imperialistas fueron permanentemente desacreditados después del éxito de las campañas militares de EE. UU. en las Filipinas.

choices.text: Hoar's Senate opposition led directly to the creation of the League of Nations in 1919 as a binding international legal mechanism to prevent future unilateral colonial conquests by powerful states.
choices.textEs: La posición de Hoar llevó directamente a la creación de la Liga de las Naciones como mecanismo internacional para prevenir futuras conquistas coloniales.

items.explanation: In the short term, Hoar's position failed — the Treaty of Paris passed and the Philippines were colonized. However, his argument about self-determination planted seeds that would recur in American foreign policy debates: Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points included self-determination as a core principle, and the gradual movement toward Philippine independence (Tydings-McDuffie Act, 1934) reflected the eventual moral victory of the non-interventionist position. The immediate policy was not changed, but the principled argument influenced future discourse. Option B is factually incorrect; Option C overstates his influence; Option D misidentifies the outcome.
items.explanationEs: A corto plazo, la posición de Hoar fracasó — el Tratado de París fue aprobado y las Filipinas fueron colonizadas. Sin embargo, su argumento sobre la autodeterminación plantó semillas que reaparecerían en los debates de política exterior americana: los Catorce Puntos de Woodrow Wilson incluyeron la autodeterminación como principio central. La opción B es factualmente incorrecta; la C exagera su influencia; la D identifica incorrectamente el resultado.

items.stem: W.E.B. Du Bois and other African American intellectuals initially took nuanced positions on American imperialism — sometimes opposing it on anti-racist grounds, sometimes seeing potential in it for Black uplift. Which of the following best explains the complexity of African American responses to imperialism?
items.stemEs: W.E.B. Du Bois y otros intelectuales afroamericanos adoptaron inicialmente posiciones matizadas sobre el imperialismo americano — a veces oponiéndose a él por razones anti-racistas, a veces viendo potencial en él para el avance de la comunidad negra. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la complejidad de las respuestas afroamericanas al imperialismo?

choices.text: African Americans universally supported American imperialism because they saw opportunities for economic advancement in colonial territories.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos apoyaron universalmente el imperialismo americano porque veían oportunidades de avance económico en los territorios coloniales.

choices.text: African Americans universally opposed American imperialism because they recognized it as an extension of the same racial oppression they faced domestically.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos se opusieron universalmente al imperialismo americano porque lo reconocieron como una extensión de la misma opresión racial que enfrentaban internamente.

choices.text: African Americans were divided, with some seeing colonial solidarity with oppressed peoples of color and others viewing imperial service as a strategic avenue for demonstrating Black citizenship and capability in a racist society.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos estaban divididos, con algunos viendo solidaridad colonial con los pueblos de color oprimidos y otros viendo el servicio imperial como una vía estratégica para demostrar la ciudadanía y capacidad negra en una sociedad racista.

choices.text: African Americans opposed imperialism primarily because they feared that colonial immigration would bring economic competition for jobs in Northern industrial cities.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos se opusieron al imperialismo principalmente porque temían que la inmigración colonial traería competencia económica por empleos en las ciudades industriales del Norte.

items.explanation: African Americans faced a genuine dilemma: they could see the racial oppression of colonized peoples as analogous to their own oppression, leading to anti-imperialist solidarity. But some also saw potential in colonial missionary and educational roles as pathways for Black Americans to demonstrate their capabilities and advance their status. Additionally, some hoped that Black soldiers' service in imperial wars might translate into greater civil rights at home — the 'Double V' logic applied earlier. This complexity reflects the strategic calculations of a marginalized group navigating a deeply racist society. Option A ignores documented anti-imperialist Black voices; Option B is false; Option D applies to a later era.
items.explanationEs: Los afroamericanos enfrentaban un dilema genuino: podían ver la opresión racial de los pueblos colonizados como análoga a su propia opresión, lo que conducía a la solidaridad anti-imperialista. Pero algunos también veían un potencial en los roles misioneros y educativos coloniales como vías para que los afroamericanos demostraran sus capacidades. Esta complejidad refleja los cálculos estratégicos de un grupo marginado. La opción A ignora las voces negras anti-imperialistas documentadas; la B es falsa; la D aplica una lógica posterior.

items.stem: The interventionist-non-interventionist debate of the 1890s–1910s resurfaced in modified form during the debate over U.S. entry into World War I. Which of the following best traces the continuity between these two debates?
items.stemEs: El debate intervencionista-no intervencionista de las décadas de 1890–1910 resurgió de forma modificada durante el debate sobre la entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones traza mejor la continuidad entre estos dos debates?

choices.text: Both debates centered on the same fundamental question: whether the United States should use military power to engage with the wider world or maintain a traditional policy of limited overseas involvement
choices.textEs: Ambos debates giraban en torno a la misma pregunta fundamental: si Estados Unidos debería usar el poder militar para involucrarse con el mundo más amplio o mantener una política tradicional de involucramiento limitado en el extranjero, y ambos involucraron la misma tensión entre intereses estratégicos, motivaciones económicas y afirmaciones morales.

choices.text: The continuity between the two debates was purely economic: both were fundamentally about whether American businesses would benefit from overseas engagement.
choices.textEs: La continuidad entre los dos debates fue puramente económica: ambos trataban fundamentalmente sobre si las empresas americanas se beneficiarían del compromiso en el extranjero.

choices.text: The continuity was purely partisan: Democrats consistently opposed intervention while Republicans consistently supported it in both debates.
choices.textEs: La continuidad fue puramente partidista: los demócratas se opusieron consistentemente a la intervención mientras que los republicanos la apoyaron consistentemente en ambos debates.

choices.text: The two debates were fundamentally different because the 1890s debate was about colonial acquisition while the WWI debate was about defending democracy, making them incomparable.
choices.textEs: Los dos debates eran fundamentalmente diferentes porque el debate de la década de 1890 era sobre la adquisición colonial mientras que el debate de la Primera Guerra Mundial era sobre la defensa de la democracia, haciéndolos incomparables.

items.explanation: The core continuity is that both debates centered on whether the United States should use military force to project power beyond its borders and whether such engagement served or undermined American interests and values. The same ideological tensions — strategic/economic interests vs. the dangers of entanglement, moral mission vs. the hypocrisy of force — appeared in both contexts. The specific actors and circumstances differed, but the underlying debate about America's role in the world was fundamentally continuous. Options B and C identify specific but incomplete aspects of the continuity; Option D creates a false dichotomy between the two debates.
items.explanationEs: La continuidad central es que ambos debates giraban en torno a si Estados Unidos debería usar la fuerza militar para proyectar poder más allá de sus fronteras y si tal compromiso servía o socavaba los intereses y valores americanos. Las mismas tensiones ideológicas — intereses estratégicos/económicos vs. los peligros del involucramiento, misión moral vs. la hipocresía de la fuerza — aparecieron en ambos contextos. Las opciones B y C identifican aspectos específicos pero incompletos de la continuidad; la D crea una falsa dicotomía entre los dos debates.

items.stem: William Jennings Bryan resigned as Secretary of State in 1915 in protest over President Wilson's response to the sinking of the Lusitania. Which of the following best evaluates Bryan's position in the context of the interventionist-non-interventionist debate?
items.stemEs: William Jennings Bryan renunció como Secretario de Estado en 1915 en protesta por la respuesta del Presidente Wilson al hundimiento del Lusitania. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la posición de Bryan en el contexto del debate intervencionista-no intervencionista?

choices.text: Bryan resigned from the State Department because he personally sympathized with Germany's position and wanted the United States to abandon neutrality and side openly with the Central Powers against Britain and France.
choices.textEs: Bryan renunció porque apoyaba personalmente a Alemania y quería que Estados Unidos se pusiera del lado de las Potencias Centrales.

choices.text: Bryan resigned as a principled non-interventionist who believed Wilson's strong protests and tolerance of American travel on belligerent ships were needlessly provoking a war the U.S. had no compelling reason to join.
choices.textEs: Bryan renunció como no intervencionista principista que creía que las fuertes protestas de Wilson y la tolerancia del viaje americano en barcos beligerantes estaban provocando innecesariamente una guerra a la que EE. UU. no tenía razón convincente para unirse.

choices.text: Bryan resigned because he believed Wilson's diplomatic tone was unnecessarily harsh toward Germany and that a more accommodating, conciliatory approach would better serve long-term American commercial and strategic interests.
choices.textEs: Bryan renunció porque creía que Wilson estaba siendo demasiado duro con Alemania y que un enfoque diplomático más conciliador serviría mejor a los intereses americanos.

choices.text: Bryan resigned strategically in order to launch a presidential campaign on an explicitly anti-war platform in 1916, using his high-profile resignation as the public opening move of his political challenge to Wilson.
choices.textEs: Bryan renunció para postularse a la presidencia en una plataforma anti-guerra en 1916, usando su renuncia como el primer movimiento de una campaña política.

items.explanation: Bryan's resignation was a principled non-interventionist act: he believed that Wilson's strong protests to Germany, combined with the continued arming of Allied ships and American citizens traveling in war zones, were deliberately provoking a conflict the U.S. should avoid. Bryan advocated warning Americans not to travel on belligerent ships as a way to stay out of the war without sacrificing national honor. He represented the traditional non-interventionist argument that the U.S. had no national interest at stake sufficient to justify war. Option A mischaracterizes Bryan's motivation; Option C confuses Bryan with pro-German sympathizers; Option D applies to a different figure.
items.explanationEs: La renuncia de Bryan fue un acto de no intervencionismo principista: creía que las fuertes protestas de Wilson a Alemania, combinadas con el continuo armamento de barcos aliados y ciudadanos americanos viajando en zonas de guerra, estaban provocando deliberadamente un conflicto que EE. UU. debería evitar. Bryan abogó por advertir a los americanos que no viajaran en barcos beligerantes. La opción A caracteriza incorrectamente la motivación de Bryan; la C lo confunde con simpatizantes pro-alemanes; la D aplica a una figura diferente.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President William McKinley's War Message to Congress, April 11, 1898 (Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain — public domain):

"The war in Cuba is of such a nature that, short of subjugation or extermination, a final military victory for either side seems impracticable... Our trade has suffered, the capital invested by our citizens in Cuba has been largely lost, and the temper and forbearance of our people have been so sorely tried as to beget a perilous unrest among our own citizens... The present condition of affairs in Cuba is a constant menace to our peace and entails upon this Government an enormous expense."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of the Spanish-American War, construct a written argument analyzing McKinley's stated justifications for U.S. intervention in Cuba. Your argument must include a claim about which justification — humanitarian, economic, or strategic — was most significant in driving the decision for war. Support your claim with at least two pieces of specific historical evidence, and use reasoning to evaluate what the excerpt reveals about McKinley's priorities. Additionally, explain how the outcomes of the war altered the United States' role in the Western Hemisphere.
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento del Mensaje de Guerra del Presidente William McKinley al Congreso, 11 de abril de 1898 (Registro del Congreso de EE. UU. — dominio público):

"La guerra en Cuba es de tal naturaleza que, salvo la subyugación o el exterminio, una victoria militar final para cualquiera de los lados parece impracticable... Nuestro comercio ha sufrido, el capital invertido por nuestros ciudadanos en Cuba se ha perdido en gran medida, y el temperamento y la paciencia de nuestro pueblo han sido tan duramente probados que han generado una inquietud peligrosa entre nuestros propios ciudadanos... La presente condición de los asuntos en Cuba es una amenaza constante para nuestra paz y supone para este Gobierno un enorme gasto."

Usando este fragmento y su conocimiento de la Guerra Hispano-Americana, construya un argumento escrito que analice las justificaciones declaradas de McKinley para la intervención de EE. UU. en Cuba. Su argumento debe incluir una afirmación sobre cuál justificación —humanitaria, económica o estratégica— fue más significativa para impulsar la decisión de ir a la guerra. Apoye su afirmación con al menos dos evidencias históricas específicas y use el razonamiento para evaluar qué revela el fragmento sobre las prioridades de McKinley. Además, explique cómo los resultados de la guerra alteraron el papel de los Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response makes a specific, defensible claim — for example: 'McKinley's message reveals that economic and strategic interests, not humanitarian concern, were the primary drivers of U.S. intervention, even though humanitarian rhetoric was used for public justification.' Evidence should include: (1) the excerpt itself — McKinley leads with trade losses and capital investment, framing Cuba as an economic and stability problem; (2) the role of the yellow press (Hearst, Pulitzer) in manufacturing humanitarian outrage, which McKinley leveraged but did not initiate; (3) the De Lôme Letter and USS Maine explosion as the domestic political trigger; (4) post-war outcomes — Platt Amendment (1901) making Cuba a de facto protectorate, Foraker Act governing Puerto Rico, and retention of the Philippines — all consistent with strategic/economic rather than purely humanitarian aims. Reasoning should explain how the Treaty of Paris (1898) transformed the U.S. from a continental power to a Pacific and Caribbean imperial power, establishing the pattern that would define the Roosevelt Corollary.

SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Makes a specific, defensible claim about the primary justification. Uses two or more specific pieces of evidence (e.g., excerpt analysis, Platt Amendment, yellow press, De Lôme Letter). Reasoning explicitly connects McKinley's language to post-war policy outcomes. Analysis explains how the war changed U.S. hemispheric role (from Monroe Doctrine passive to active interventionism via Platt Amendment / Roosevelt Corollary trajectory).
3 - Proficient: Clear claim present. Two relevant pieces of evidence, at least one specific. Reasoning connects McKinley's message to the war's outcomes but may stop short of explaining the broader hemispheric role shift.
2 - Developing: Claim is vague. One specific piece of evidence. Limited reasoning that mainly summarizes the excerpt rather than analyzing it. Hemispheric role change mentioned but underdeveloped.
1 - Beginning: No clear claim. Evidence is vague or absent. Response mostly retells the Spanish-American War without analytical engagement with the excerpt.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: McKinley's economic framing in the excerpt; De Lôme Letter (February 1898); USS Maine explosion (February 15, 1898); yellow press (Hearst / Pulitzer); Treaty of Paris (1898) — territories acquired; Teller Amendment (no annexation of Cuba) vs. Platt Amendment (1901) protectorate status; Foraker Act (1900) for Puerto Rico; shift from Monroe Doctrine passivity to active intervention.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Formula una afirmación específica y defendible sobre la justificación principal. Usa dos o más evidencias específicas (p. ej., análisis del fragmento, Enmienda Platt, prensa amarilla, Carta De Lôme). El razonamiento conecta explícitamente el lenguaje de McKinley con los resultados de la política de posguerra. El análisis explica cómo la guerra cambió el papel hemisférico de EE. UU. (de la doctrina Monroe pasiva al intervencionismo activo).
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara presente. Dos evidencias relevantes, al menos una específica. El razonamiento conecta el mensaje de McKinley con los resultados de la guerra pero puede no explicar completamente el cambio de papel hemisférico.
2 - En desarrollo: La afirmación es vaga. Una evidencia específica. Razonamiento limitado que principalmente resume el fragmento en lugar de analizarlo.
1 - Inicial: Sin afirmación clara. Evidencia vaga o ausente. La respuesta mainly retrata la Guerra Hispano-Americana sin análisis.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera de tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Marco económico de McKinley; Carta De Lôme (febrero 1898); explosión del USS Maine (15 feb. 1898); prensa amarilla; Tratado de París (1898); Enmienda Teller vs. Enmienda Platt (1901); Ley Foraker (1900); cambio de la Doctrina Monroe pasiva al intervencionismo activo.

items.stem: Following the Spanish-American War, the Supreme Court's Insular Cases (1901) ruled that the Constitution did not automatically apply in full to newly acquired territories like the Philippines and Puerto Rico. How does the Court's creation of 'unincorporated territory' status expose a fundamental tension within American democratic principles?

choices.text: The Supreme Court correctly ruled that all territories eventually incorporated into the United States would receive full constitutional protections, making the unincorporated status a temporary practical arrangement rather than a permanent denial of rights.

The decisions revealed that Congress had overstepped its constitutional authority by acquiring overseas territories without clear authorization, forcing the Court to construct an ad hoc legal framework to manage a fundamentally unconstitutional expansion of American jurisdiction.

By ruling that the Constitution did not automatically follow the flag into unincorporated territories, the Court created a category of people subject to American governance and taxation without the constitutional protections that governance is supposed to guarantee — directly contradicting the founding principle that just government derives its authority from the consent of the governed

The Insular Cases resolved the constitutional question cleanly by treating newly acquired territories as sovereign entities in a special protective relationship with the United States, allowing flexible governance without triggering the full constitutional obligations attached to formal American territories.

items.explanation: The Insular Cases created a constitutionally anomalous situation in which millions of people came under permanent American governmental authority without receiving the full constitutional protections American governance was theoretically founded upon, exposing a contradiction between democratic ideology and imperial governance.

items.stem:
Document-Based Question: The Spanish-American War and the Question of Empire, 1898

Directions: Read the three documents below. Then write a well-organized essay that constructs an argument addressing the following question: Did the Spanish-American War represent a turning point in American foreign policy, or was it the inevitable product of forces already at work in American society and politics?

Your essay must:
— Apply SOAPS analysis (Speaker, Occasion, Audience, Purpose, Significance) to at least two of the three documents
— Use evidence from all three documents
— Incorporate outside knowledge of the period
— Construct a clear, defensible argument

---
DOCUMENT 1
President William McKinley, War Message to Congress, April 11, 1898 — Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain, public domain:
"The present condition of affairs in Cuba is a constant menace to our peace and entails upon this Government an enormous expense. With such a conflict waged for years in an island so near our border and with which our people have such trade and business relations; when the lives and liberty of our citizens are in constant danger and their property destroyed and themselves ruined; where our trading vessels are liable to seizure and are seized at our very door by warships of a foreign nation — the expedient of enforcing American interests will justify forceful intervention."

---
DOCUMENT 2
Teller Amendment, April 20, 1898, Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain — public domain:
"Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives... That the United States hereby disclaims any disposition or intention to exercise sovereignty, jurisdiction, or control over said Island except for the pacification thereof, and asserts its determination, when that is accomplished, to leave the government and control of the Island to its people."

---
DOCUMENT 3
Platt Amendment, 1901, Statutes at Large of the United States — public domain:
"The government of Cuba consents that the United States may exercise the right to intervene for the preservation of Cuban independence, the maintenance of a government adequate for protecting life, property, and individual liberty, and for discharging the obligations with respect to Cuba imposed by the Treaty of Paris on the United States... Cuba will sell or lease to the United States lands necessary for coaling or naval stations at certain specified points to be agreed upon with the President of the United States."
items.stemEs:
Pregunta Basada en Documentos: La Guerra Hispano-Americana y la Cuestión del Imperio, 1898

Instrucciones: Lea los tres documentos a continuación. Luego escriba un ensayo bien organizado que construya un argumento que aborde la siguiente pregunta: ¿Representó la Guerra Hispano-Americana un punto de inflexión en la política exterior estadounidense, o fue el producto inevitable de fuerzas ya en acción en la sociedad y la política estadounidenses?

Su ensayo debe:
— Aplicar el análisis SOAPS (Orador, Ocasión, Audiencia, Propósito, Significado) a al menos dos de los tres documentos
— Utilizar evidencia de los tres documentos
— Incorporar conocimiento externo del período
— Construir un argumento claro y defendible

---
DOCUMENTO 1
Presidente William McKinley, Mensaje de Guerra al Congreso, 11 de abril de 1898 — Registro del Congreso de EE. UU., dominio público:
"La presente condición de los asuntos en Cuba es una amenaza constante para nuestra paz y supone para este Gobierno un enorme gasto. Con tal conflicto librado durante años en una isla tan cercana a nuestra frontera y con la que nuestro pueblo tiene tales relaciones comerciales y de negocios; cuando las vidas y la libertad de nuestros ciudadanos están en peligro constante y su propiedad destruida y ellos mismos arruinados; donde nuestros barcos mercantes son susceptibles de incautación y son incautados a nuestra misma puerta por buques de guerra de una nación extranjera — el expediente de hacer cumplir los intereses americanos justificará la intervención forzosa."

---
DOCUMENTO 2
Enmienda Teller, 20 de abril de 1898, Registro del Congreso de EE. UU. — dominio público:
"Resuelto por el Senado y la Cámara de Representantes... Que los Estados Unidos por la presente reniegan de cualquier disposición o intención de ejercer soberanía, jurisdicción o control sobre dicha Isla excepto para la pacificación de la misma, y afirman su determinación, cuando se logre eso, de dejar el gobierno y control de la Isla a su pueblo."

---
DOCUMENTO 3
Enmienda Platt, 1901, Estatutos Generales de los Estados Unidos — dominio público:
"El gobierno de Cuba consiente en que los Estados Unidos puedan ejercer el derecho de intervenir para la preservación de la independencia de Cuba, el mantenimiento de un gobierno adecuado para proteger la vida, la propiedad y la libertad individual, y para cumplir las obligaciones respecto a Cuba impuestas por el Tratado de París a los Estados Unidos... Cuba venderá o arrendará a los Estados Unidos tierras necesarias para estaciones de carbón o navales en ciertos puntos especificados a acordar con el Presidente de los Estados Unidos."
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (6/6) response presents a complex, defensible thesis — such as: 'The Spanish-American War was both a turning point and an inevitable product of prior forces: it accelerated an imperial trajectory already shaped by Mahan's sea-power theory, economic expansion, and Social Darwinism, but the pivot from the Teller Amendment's anti-annexation promise (Document 2) to the Platt Amendment's protectorate structure (Document 3) represents a genuine and consequential policy turn.' SOAPS analysis for at least two documents: Document 1 (McKinley War Message) — Speaker: sitting president; Occasion: formal request for a declaration of war; Audience: Congress and the American public; Purpose: justify intervention by framing it as defensive of American commercial and citizen interests; Significance: framing of the war as economic/strategic rather than humanitarian reveals the priorities behind the public humanitarian narrative. Document 2 (Teller Amendment) — Speaker: U.S. Congress; Occasion: declaration of war authorization; Audience: American public, Cuba, and Spain; Purpose: preclude accusations of imperial annexation; Significance: its promise was immediately contradicted by post-war policy, revealing the gap between stated intentions and imperial outcomes. Document 3 (Platt Amendment) — Speaker: U.S. Congress, 1901; Occasion: post-war governance of Cuba; Audience: Cuban government and people; Purpose: establish permanent U.S. rights of intervention and naval basing; Significance: effectively negated Teller and established the protectorate system that would govern U.S.-Cuba relations until 1934. Cross-document synthesis: the evolution from Teller to Platt demonstrates that even when Congress explicitly disclaimed imperial intentions, strategic and economic logic drove imperial outcomes. Outside knowledge: USS Maine, yellow press, Dewey at Manila Bay, Treaty of Paris, Philippine acquisition, Cuba's de facto protectorate status 1901–1934, Roosevelt Corollary as the legal follow-on.

SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Complex thesis addressing both 'turning point' and 'inevitable product' dimensions. SOAPS analysis of at least two documents accurately and specifically. Cross-document synthesis (Teller → Platt contradiction). Extensive outside knowledge. Well-organized argumentative essay.
5 - Advanced: Clear thesis. SOAPS applied to at least two documents accurately. Good outside knowledge. Addresses the Teller/Platt contradiction but may not fully develop the 'turning point vs. inevitable' framework.
4 - Proficient: Clear thesis. Uses all three documents as evidence. SOAPS applied to at least two documents with reasonable accuracy. Some outside knowledge. Coherent argument.
3 - Adequate: Thesis present but simple. Uses two or more documents. Some SOAPS elements. Limited outside knowledge. Some organizational issues.
2 - Developing: Weak or no thesis. Uses one or two documents without SOAPS. Little outside knowledge. Descriptive rather than argumentative.
1 - Beginning: No thesis. Minimal document use. No SOAPS. No outside knowledge.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS:
— Doc 1: McKinley's economic/commercial framing; distinguish from humanitarian yellow-press justification; note 'enforcing American interests' as the operative phrase.
— Doc 2: Teller's explicit anti-annexation intent; note its unanimous passage alongside the war authorization; significance = set up later contradiction with Platt.
— Doc 3: Platt's intervention rights and naval basing provisions; note this was imposed as a condition of U.S. military withdrawal; Cuba had no real choice; significance = established protectorate in all but name.
